# Review — ani-147-a (Spell 147, gates 1–3, Plate 11)

## Pass 1

All edits were made by script (`review1.py` in the reviewer's scratchpad: json load/dump, ensure_ascii=False, indent 1). Afterwards a script checked that the 740 glyph codes, joined in order, are exactly the established sequence, that every unit has an int `ln`, that every `ln` is the established line of the unit's first glyph, that the rubric flags match the established words, and that every `q` matches the established layout (or is the correct re-index for the six joins and splits the notes report). All checks passed.

Counts: 1 major, 17 minor, 5 style.

### Changes

- U1, U2, U3, U8, U22, U24, U32, U33, U34 (the `n` after `rn`) and U20 (`nt`) · morph lemma · major · the genitive "of" was keyed to lemma `n`, so the glossary would have shown "not; negates the verb" under these 10 words. Every published part keys the genitive as `ny` ("of (the genitive adjective; written n, fem. nt …)") · re-keyed to `ny`.
- U23 · l, n · minor · `l` had "of" for a word that is not written (hall 2 l. 3 has `rn sꜣwty·s` with no n) · `l` now "the-name-of · watcher-its"; the note says this is the direct genitive.
- U12 w63 `mꜣꜣ·n·k`, U30 w160 `mꜣꜣ` · glyphs role/tr · minor · eye coded `log mꜣꜣ` and sickle `comp mꜣ`, against the house analysis of the eye-and-sickle ligature (sickle `phon mꜣ`, eye `det`; ani-125-address, ani-125-introduction, ani-hymn-to-ra, ani-017-c) · recoded D4 det "", U1 phon mꜣ. - U0 w1, U4 w23 · reading, say, n · minor · reading `tpt` and the note "the ordinal from tp". The house reading gives the word meant (`tpy` in hymn-to-osiris, "its y unwritten"). tpy is the nisba adjective that serves as "first", not an ordinal in -nw · reading `tpyt`, say `tepyt`; both notes say which endings are not written.
- U0 · n · style · ꜥryt is rendered "gate" here, but ani-125-address rendered it "lintel" · added a sentence: there the word names a part of a door; here, with the house sign, it is a whole gate(house).
- U4 · n · style · Budge reads t'eṭtu (the strokes as passive -tw), and the note did not mention it · one clause added: "the sense is the same", as in ani-001-a.
- U5 (nudge in U43) · n · minor · O42 has tr šsp under the reading sšp, and the note did not say that the s is not written (ani-022-072 says so) · added.
- U8 · l, n · minor · `i` has "Draw me on!", but `l` had no "(me)". The note did not say that `irt`, with its t, is not the negatival complement expected after `imi` · `l` now "draw-on-(me)"; one clause added to the doubt.
- U10 · n · minor · footnote 2: the note said Budge's sceptre "is what the signs here show", although Budge's footnote says that the papyrus has im·k. The sceptre is Budge's own correction from l. 5, not what Ani's scribe wrote · rewritten to say so plainly. The signs are kept as Budge prints them (as the established sequence requires), and sḫm·k is followed with the warning.
- U10 · i · minor · `l` "have-power-may-you" (sḏm·f as a wish), but `i` "and have power" (imperative force) · `i` now "Raise yourself; may you have power, Osiris, in Abydos!"
- U11 · l · style · "[tw]": square brackets are used in this house for restorations, and untranslated words go in round brackets ("(iw)" in weighing-of-the-heart) · "(tw)".

- U18 · n · minor · grammatical label "wḏꜥ, a sḏm·f after nty". A sḏm·f after nty needs its own subject, and none is written · the note now says that the form is unclear and that "who judges" takes nty as the subject.

### Drafter's open points — rulings

- **Footnote 2 at w53 (S42 G17 V31 read sḫm·k):** kept. The established signs are Budge's print and cannot change. The papyrus's im·k makes no sense here, and the parallel in l. 5 supports sḫm·k. The note now says plainly that the sceptre is Budge's correction (see changes).
- **ꜥryt "gate":** kept. With the house determinative O1 the word is a gate-building, not a door-part, and "hall" is Budge's. "Gate" also stays distinct from sbḫt "pylon" (Spell 146, lower register) if that is rendered "pylon". The known entry is too narrow and needs broadening (below). The note now covers the "lintel" rendering in ani-125-address.
- **Run of infinitives, hall 1 ll. 13–17:** kept. `irt` (w96, with t) is an infinitive, and wp / snḏm / sḫn fit a list of deeds. The sḏm·n·f alternative from hall 3 is now in the U17 note.
- **Missing first-person suffixes in hall 3:** changed to house practice (reading with ·i, `l` "-(I)"; see changes).
- **mꜣꜥtyw at w140 (packet w142):** reading kept as a marked guess. The misused "papyrus writes / read" formula was removed. `i` keeps "(?)".
- **Unwritten ordinal endings:** readings give the word meant (snnwt, ḫmtnwt kept; tpt → tpyt). The notes say what is not written.

### Considered and refused

- U17 w89, U41 · V28 (wick ḥ shape) given tr "nḏm" in snḏm: kept. The sign is coded approximately, the type shows a twisted shape, Budge reads no ḥ, and the note says the reading rests on taking it as the nḏm sign. Recoding it as ḥ would leave an impossible word.
- U7 w35 · N37 given tr "ḏw" in rḏw·k: kept. The note opens with the misprint formula. Aa2 and Budge's footnote 1 leave only one sense (rḏw "efflux"), so the formula is right here.
- U38 · "The papyrus writes ꜣ t (sun) ·f; read iꜣt·f": kept. ꜣt "moment" gives no sense after wnḫ, and iꜣt·f in hall 3 l. 8 and Budge's "standard" agree, so the formula is legitimate.
- U36 w186 · reading `gb` under lemma `qbb`: kept as written. Unlike gꜣḥ, getting qbb means changing g to q and adding a b, so it is a real reinterpretation and doubtful. The signs are left as the reading, and the note says "doubtful".
- Double reed tr "y","y" in sꜣwty·s / iryw against "i","i" in ꜥryt: not changed. The house uses both (ꜥnḫyw y,y in ani-125-address; ꜥryt i,i), and the draft follows each precedent.
- U17–U19 · `i` written as participial fragments ("Opening the way …,"): kept. The Egyptian is a list of infinitives with no main verb, and inventing one ("I am the one …") would add to the text.
- U16 · `i` "There is no opposing me at it, at his wall of burning coals" is close in structure to Budge's line: kept. It follows the word order, and Budge's own words ("repulse") are not used.
- U34 · name Aa keyed to lemma `ꜥꜣ` with its own occurrence gloss: kept. A separate key would collide with the reading, and the occurrence gloss gives the name and Budge's Āaa.
- U8 · Rosetau "near Memphis" (note) against "near Giza" (glossary): not a contradiction; not changed.
- `titleEn` "part 1" against parts.json "first half": kept, as it follows the ani-017-* pattern. ani-147-b should use "part 2".
- Repeated `ln` values across halls: per the 2026-11-22 ruling in QUESTIONS.md.
- A2 (hand to mouth) as classifier of rn / smi, and A52 in Ani's name: as established. The established sequence cannot change.
- U25 · reading `tn` as "this (gate)" with the noun unwritten, and U26 rubric words said to belong to the speech: kept. Both are stated as doubtful in the notes, and no better reading is supported by the signs.

### For the glosser

Lemmas used that are not in known-lemmas.json: gꜣḥ, hꜣ-ḫrw, mkt, mtty-ḥ, mꜣꜥtyw, qbb, qq-ḥwꜣwt-nt-pḥwy, rnpt, rḏw, smnḫ, snḏm, spr, sqd-ḥr, srs-ḥr, sḫd-ḥr-ꜥšꜣ-irw, sḫḫ, sṯꜣ, wn-ḥꜣt, wsd, ḏꜥbt, ḫmt, ḫmtnw. Names take Budge's spelling in brackets: Sekhet-ḥrà-āsht-àru, Metti-heh, Ha-kheru, Un-ḥāt, Seqeṭ-ḥrà, Useṭ, Qeq-ḥauatu-ent-peḥui, Se-res-ḥrà.

Known entries too narrow for this part (`__broaden__`):
- ꜥryt — add: gate, gateway, gatehouse (one of the gates of the realm of Osiris, Spell 147; with the house sign).
- smi — add: announcer, herald (noun; the being who announces whoever arrives at a gate).
- sḫn — add: to embrace (with the embracing arms D32).
- imi — add: a second word of the same spelling: the negative verb "do not, you are not to" (imi + suffix + negatival complement; im·k).
- wnḫ — add: to clothe, dress (a person or a cult object, e.g. a standard).
